# /fc:current

[← Back to commands](../commands.md)

<!-- Generated by skills/ai-layout/scripts/sync-docs.js from commands/current.md; do not edit. Edit docs/commands/_notes/current.md instead. -->

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Claude name | `/fc:current` |
| Codex name | `$fc-current` |
| Kind | Plugin-level command — works in any repo |
| Description | List only the plans in progress — started but not finished — with each plan's progress and the next step to pick up; --spec &lt;id&gt; narrows it to one spec's plans |
| Arguments | `[--spec <id>]` |

## Usage

Run it when you want to see only the work under way: the plans with at least one step ticked or started and at least one step still open. Each plan gets one row with its progress (ticked steps out of the steps not withdrawn) and the next step to pick up — the first open step `/fc:loop` could start now, or else the first open step. Plans not started yet, finished plans and plans in `ai-factory/plans/done/` are left out. It reads the files on disk, so the answer is the same twice running. It is read-only and asks nothing.

| Argument | Lists |
|---|---|
| none | every plan in progress |
| `--spec <id>` | only the plans in progress whose `**Spec:**` line names that spec |

A plan whose step lines cannot be interpreted is listed as `unreadable`, with the reason beside it, whatever its steps say.

See also: [`/fc:state`](state.md) for everything outstanding, including specs and plans not started yet.

## Examples

```
/fc:current
/fc:current --spec ASD-006
$fc-current
```

## Writes

Nothing: terminal output only. It edits no file, ticks no box, moves no plan and starts no step or agent. The `current` row in the run log is written by the plugin's `log-task.js` hook, as for every command.

## Refuses or asks

It never asks. Any argument other than `--spec <id>` — such as `--done`, a bare ID, `--spec` with no ID or a second `--spec` — is refused in one line naming `--spec <id>`, and that line is the answer. With no plan in progress, no `ai-factory/plans/` directory or no plan for the spec, it answers in one line instead of a table.
